Synopsis:
Australia's federal government is pushing for binding national standards requiring new datacentres to run on 100% renewable electricity, clashing with Queensland and NT governments who prefer using state-owned gas/coal assets. The article argues the real issue is structural: Australia is not building renewable energy infrastructure fast enough to meet accelerating electricity demand — from datacentres (17% of future demand growth), EVs, electrification, and population growth. The author advocates for restricting electricity emissions broadly and accelerating infrastructure build-out (renewables, transmission, storage, backup generation).
